about: A touchscreen: what it registers with (beside an e-paper screen's registration, the same route) and is answered, what GET /api/devices/config answers (a touchscreen is paired by token, so never has a pairing code), and what it saves with PUT /api/devices/config from its own settings panel (`save`: the whole config as it got it, its skin and sleep changed, read-only fields and all), what it saves a section at a time with PUT /api/devices/config/{section} (`section_save`: the section's name, the version it was changed from as If-Match, the section whole, and the config answered with its new version), and what GET /api/devices/spotify/token answers it once paired (`spotify_token`: an access token for its owner's Spotify). It can register through the login instead, at the settings site's /register (`register`: the query it opens, with its secret's hash, and `registered_return` and `taken_return`, where the page sends it back to). The touchscreen's tests check its client against these, and the broker's tests its routes. An e-paper screen's config is config_store.json's. The store contract's canonical example (countdown-api's countdown_api/fixtures), which every consumer's tests read: change it there.

spotify_token.scope: streaming user-read-email user-read-private user-read-playback-state user-modify-playback-state user-read-currently-playing user-library-read user-read-recently-played playlist-read-private user-top-read
